title: Data centre electricity use surged in 2025, even with tightening bottlenecks driving a scramble for solutions
date_evidence: IEA news release on 'Key Questions on Energy and AI' published 22 April 2026; reports 2025 data centre electricity demand up 17% and AI-focused data centres up 50% year-on-year.
key_claim: Data centre electricity demand surged 17 percent in 2025 with AI-focused data centres growing 50 percent; the IEA expects total data-centre electricity consumption to double by 2030, with AI-focused use tripling; the binding constraint is now physical (grids, transformer lead times, gas turbines, uranium) rather than digital.
verbatim_quote: The constraint is physical, not digital.
notes: Tier 1 IEA flagship anchor for the energy-as-binding-constraint thesis.

title: Large Energy User Connection Policy - Decision Paper (CRU2025236)
date_evidence: CRU decision-paper code 'CRU2025236' encodes the 2025 decision year; the decision was published 11 December 2025 (Politico Pro confirms 15 December 2025 Politico coverage of the end of the de-facto moratorium); system-operator publication of connection rules due 31 March 2026 under this policy.
key_claim: Ireland ended a three-year de-facto moratorium on grid connections for new data centres; new data centres must source at least 80 percent of annual demand via additional renewable generation in the Republic of Ireland and provide dispatchable onsite or proximate generation matching their Maximum Import Capacity; System Operators required to publish connection rules by 31 March 2026.
notes: Tier 1 Irish sovereign regulator decision; structural anchor used because it is the canonical primary source for the grid-eligibility rule despite sitting just outside the soft 3-month window (Dec 11 2025 to Jun 2 2026).

title: Singapore Announces Data Center Capacity Allocation Call (DC-CFA2)
date_evidence: Morgan Lewis client alert dated March 2026; URL contains '/2026/03/' confirming the publication month; covers IMDA DC-CFA2 application window (1 December 2025 launch, 31 March 2026 application deadline).
key_claim: Singapore's second Data Centre-Call for Application released only 200MW of new capacity (more than double the 2022 pilot's 80MW) with hard sustainability and efficiency floors: at least 50 percent powered by eligible green pathways, BCA-IMDA Green Mark Platinum, PUE 1.25 or better, compliance with SS 715:2025; the application window closed 31 March 2026.
notes: Tier 2 law-firm analysis; the most accessible single source for the DC-CFA2 quota and conditions.

title: DIFC to become the world's first AI-Native financial centre
date_evidence: DIFC news release dated 21 April 2026; companion PR Newswire release (prnewswire.com/news-releases/difc-to-become-the-worlds-first-ai-native-financial-centre-302748546.html) carries the same date.
key_claim: DIFC announced 21 April 2026 that it will become the world's first AI-Native financial centre, embedding AI at the foundational level of its legal frameworks, business environment, talent development, ecosystem infrastructure and physical urban fabric; programme projected to generate USD 3.5bn (AED 12.9bn) in economic benefits and 25,000 jobs.
notes: Tier 4 centre-authority release; treat the 'world's first' framing and the headline economic-benefit numbers directionally because the centre has a commercial incentive in the announcement.

title: It's time to start treating AI infrastructure as critical infrastructure
date_evidence: WEF Stories article published 2 April 2026; URL contains '/2026/04/' confirming publication month; article references March 2026 Iranian drone strikes on AWS facilities in UAE and Bahrain as the precipitating event.
key_claim: Modern AI infrastructure now requires massive capital intensity and energy capacity and is evolving from data storage into a strategic national utility; in March 2026 Iranian drones struck AWS facilities in UAE and Bahrain, marking the first time commercial hyperscale data centres became explicit kinetic targets in modern conflict; the Gulf is the revealing test case because it sits at the intersection of AI demand, capital and energy availability, and strategic contestation.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank framing; binding for the 'AI infrastructure is critical infrastructure' thesis and the Gulf test-case argument.

title: Tracking Trillions: The Assumptions Shaping the Scale of the AI Build-Out
date_evidence: Goldman Sachs Insights article published early May 2026 (BigGo Finance and Fortune coverage citing the report appeared 6 May 2026); the report sizes capex 2026-2031 at approximately USD 7.6 trillion across compute, data centres and power.
key_claim: Goldman Sachs estimates roughly USD 7.6 trillion of AI capital expenditure 2026-2031 across compute (USD 5.1tn), data centres (USD 2.15tn) and power (USD 358bn); the final scale is highly sensitive to a small set of assumptions about chip depreciation lifecycle and grid capacity rather than to demand.
notes: Tier 2 investment-bank research; treat the USD 7.6tn aggregate directionally because Goldman's framing carries commercial incentive in framing AI as a multi-year investible theme.

title: What the world can learn from Ireland's battle to power data centres
date_evidence: Irish Times article published 17 March 2026; URL contains '/2026/03/17/' encoding the publication date; article frames Ireland's CRU policy reset as a template other jurisdictions are studying.
key_claim: Ireland's three-year battle to balance data-centre growth against grid capacity has become a study case other European centres are watching; the resolution (the December 2025 CRU policy) trades open-ended growth for a strict 80-percent-renewable, dispatchable-onsite-generation regime; other European hubs facing similar power pressures include London, Amsterdam and Frankfurt.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism; useful as the centre-policy implication framing and as the cross-jurisdiction comparison anchor.

publisher: Bank for International Settlements (Christina Papaconstantinou speech)
title: Implementation status of key regulations - DORA, MiCAR, Basel IV, Genius Act and the AI Act - and what early enforcement reveals
date_evidence: BIS Review publication code 'r251031h' encodes 31 October 2025 publication date; speech delivered by Bank of Greece Deputy Governor Christina Papaconstantinou covering early enforcement of DORA (live January 2025), MiCAR, Basel IV, the GENIUS Act (signed July 2025) and the EU AI Act (full application August 2026).
key_claim: DORA requires EU banks to demonstrate concentration-risk assessment and independent operational capability without vendor dependency; the EU AI Act reaches full application 2 August 2026 with penalties up to 7 percent of global annual revenue for violations of high-risk AI rules in finance; combined effect drives banks to repatriate workloads and prefer sovereign-AI compute paths.
notes: Tier 1 central-bank speech anchor for the DORA + AI Act + sovereign-AI link to centre eligibility. Outside the soft 3-month window so flagged is_structural_anchor=true; second of the two anchors used in this scan (CRU Ireland is the other).
